כֵּנִים (kenim) передано одним словом «честные» во всех стихах (42.31, 33, 34) и в комментариях, как в Синодальном («люди честные»), чтобы повтор слова был виден читателю.
אֵינֶנּוּ — «нет его» без причины; Синодальное «не стало» добавляет оттенок исчезновения, поэтому в буквальном слое «нет его», в драматическом «его больше нет».
רַעֲבוֹן בָּתֵּיכֶם: в буквальном слое — «голод домов ваших», как в иврите; в драматическом — «что нужно вашим домам против голода». Синодальный добавляет «хлеб», в буквальном слое это не добавлено.
תִּסְחָרוּ: в буквальном слое «будете ходить [по торговым делам]»; Синодальный — «промышлять». Для драматического слоя взято «торговать», как в английском слое.

В буквальном слое «תָּמִית» дано формой «умертвишь» (хифиль, «ты можешь предать смерти»), чтобы сохранить причинный оттенок корня; Синодальное «убей» — повелительное наклонение, которого в иврите здесь нет.

history.note: [consider] Consider «близкое к клятве с заранее названной карой» or «самопроклятие, почти клятва». (GEN.42.37: "אֶת־שְׁנֵי בָנַי תָּמִית")

agent_notes: Шеол в литературном слое передан как «Шеол», в соответствии с уже принятым в книге написанием (loc.sheol); Синодальный перевод ставит «во гроб», как и KJV «the grave». Это отмечено в комментарии.
אָסוֹן передано как «беда» в литературном слое и «несчастье, грозящее жизни» в комментарии: Синодальное «несчастье» слабее, чем древнееврейское слово, которое означает гибельный удар.
הַשַּׁלִּיט — «властитель»; Синодальное «начальник» названо в комментарии.

Игра корня נכר (узнал / сделал себя чужим / не узнали) передана повтором «узнал… сделал себя чужим»; в литературном слое «притворился чужим», в буквальном — «сделал себя чужим». Синодальное «показал, будто не знает их» сглаживает повтор корня.
עֶרְוַת הָאָרֶץ — «нагота земли», как в Синодальном переводе; в литературном слое «где земля не защищена», без добавления фактов.

[event:evt.gen_42.sacks_filled_and_departure] Causal edges to the lodging find and the emptied sacks were added (42:25 is the cause of both 42:28 and 42:35).

[event:evt.gen_42.brothers_bow_to_joseph] Considered linking 42:6 to the sheaf dream (37:7) and the star dream (37:9) as FULFILLS_PROPHECY. Only the sheaf dream is linked: the star dream involves Jacob and Joseph's mother and is not fulfilled by this scene. Confidence 0.8 because dreams are not stated as divine words in ch. 37. The dream is completed in full only when the whole family bows (ch. 46-47).

[event:evt.gen_42.brothers_confess_guilt] Placed on the same day as the third-day speech, right after 'and they did so' (42:20). The Hebrew gives no gap. Verse 23 (the interpreter) is circumstantial and stays in this event.

[event:evt.gen_42.simeon_bound] Simeon is taken, bound before their eyes, and kept as hostage. Reuben's rebuke (42:22) is in the confession event. A later chapter (43:23) releases Simeon; the chronologist of GEN.43 should write the link.
[entity:group.joseph_brothers] Used for the ten brothers who go to Egypt, including Reuben and Simeon, who are also listed separately where they act or are acted on alone.

[entity:deity.yhwh] 'The God' (ha-elohim) in 42:18 and 'God' in 42:28 are mapped to deity.yhwh as MENTIONED, following the instruction that a divine title is the deity. Joseph's 'fear of God' in 42:18 is spoken by an Egyptian official in character.
[system:sys.binding_oath] Reused for Joseph's oath by the life of Pharaoh (42:15–16); this is an oath by the king rather than by the LORD, so sys.oath_by_yhwh was not used.
[entity:person.benjamin] Defined here though he is born in Gen 35, because the corpus begins at Gen 37 and he is first mentioned in this chapter's text (42:4). tipnr_id taken from the registry.
[entity:person.simeon] First mention in the corpus is 42:24, though he is named at Gen 34 in the wider text; tipnr from the registry.

[entity:person.interpreter_of_joseph] Unnamed figure inferred from 42:23, which says an interpreter stood between Joseph and his brothers. I placed him as PRESENT in the dialogues up to the confession (42:9–23) by inference; the text only states his presence in v23.
[entity:artifact.returned_silver] Defined as an artifact because the plot turns on the silver being found twice (42:27, 42:35). Not a precise quantity: the text speaks of each man's bundle.
[entity:group.joseph_brothers] Used for the ten brothers who go to Egypt, including Reuben and Simeon, who are also listed separately where they act or are acted on alone.

[entity:deity.yhwh] 'The God' (ha-elohim) in 42:18 and 'God' in 42:28 are mapped to deity.yhwh as MENTIONED, following the instruction that a divine title is the deity. Joseph's 'fear of God' in 42:18 is spoken by an Egyptian official in character.
[event_links:evt.gen_42.brothers_go_down] No location given: the event covers the journey (42:3), Benjamin's staying (42:4) and arrival in Egypt (42:5), so no single place fits.
[event_links:evt.gen_42.brothers_bow_to_joseph] Located in Egypt, but the city is unnamed in the text (Joseph's seat is not stated), so loc.egypt is used. loc.canaan is MENTIONED only (42:7).
[event_links:evt.gen_42.money_found_at_lodging] Place left out: the text says only 'the lodging place' on the road back, with no name or coordinates.
[event_links:evt.gen_42.jacob_urges_descent] Located in Canaan by carry-over from 42:5 and 42:13; the text does not name Jacob's residence here.
[component:comp.joseph.identity.1] Inferred state from 42:7–8; it persists beyond this chapter until Joseph reveals himself in Gen 45.
[component:comp.israel.protectiveness.1] Inferred from Jacob's stated fear in 42:4 and 42:38. Opened at 42:4 although the speech is reported in the narrator's voice. Left open for the next chapter.
[component:comp.simeon.custody.1] Left open: Simeon is still held at the end of the chapter and is released in a later chapter.
[system:sys.binding_oath] Reused for Joseph's oath by the life of Pharaoh (42:15–16); this is an oath by the king rather than by the LORD, so sys.oath_by_yhwh was not used.
[system:sys.espionage_accusation] Defined rather than reused: no existing system covers a suspicion of spying. Whether Joseph believes the charge or is staging a test is left to the commentary.
[system:sys.hostage_surety] Defined for Simeon's detention (42:19, 42:24). Joseph first proposes 'one of you' stay bound (42:19), then selects Simeon.
[system:sys.famine_grain_sale] Defined as a recurring practice, because Gen 41:56 and 42:6 both show Joseph selling grain.
[event_links:evt.gen_42.sacks_filled_and_departure] The brothers who 'filled' the vessels (42:25) are unnamed Egyptian servants; no entity was created for them.
